newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, COURIER SEARCHING FOR FORM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS, COURIER SEARCHING FOR FORM.

text.p: Former men's champions Jim Courier and Pete Sampras struggled for form in the Australian Open on Thursday as the top women sailed into the third round.

World number one Sampras conceded he had entered the danger zone of the US$7.6 million grand slam tournament after a hesitant four-set win over Romanian Adrian Voinea. Courier had five bruising sets against Slava Dosedel of the Czech Republic.
Sampras said he felt out of sorts at the start of his centre court struggle with 48th ranked Voinea, who played with nothing to lose.
"I didn't play too well," top seed Sampras said after pulling himself together to wrap up the match 3-6 6-2 6-3 6-2 with 14 aces.
He now faces in-form Australian Mark Woodforde, a semifinalist here last year, for a place in the final 16.

Woodforde, who has an impressive list of upset wins over the past 12 months, hopes to repeat the feat of compatriot Mark Philippoussis who last year knocked Sampras out of the Open in the third round.
"He is very capable of beating me," said Sampras of the 28th ranked Woodforde.
Courier, a former world number one climbing back up the rankings after a disappointing 1996, was at his belligerent best in a 3-1/2 hours tussle with Dosedel, ranked world number 67.
"I think this year I have played as well as I've ever played," said Courier, who has a history of clawing his way through grand slam draws with five-set wins.
By contrast, third-seeded Croat Goran Ivanisevic needed only 89 minutes to dispose of Karol Kucera of Slovakia 6-4 6-2 6-2 in a night match.
Fifth seed Thomas Muster of Austria and Spanish 10th seed Albert Costa also powered into the third round in straight sets, as did the top women's seeds.
Swiss Martina Hingis and eighth seed Irina Spirlea were both straight sets winners, while second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario did not have time to raise a sweat before her opponent retired hurt.
Sanchez Vicario was a game ahead three minutes into the match when Belgian Stephanie de Ville twisted an ankle and was taken from the court in a wheelchair.

Germany's Anke Huber, whose mother added her name to the injury list when she mysteriously collapsed here on Wednesday, also won through, although Italy's Francesca Lubiani gave the world number five a fright by taking the first set 6-4.
"She's doing fine and she's coming back this afternoon from hospital and everything was okay," said Huber, whose second round match was postponed because of the incident.
Hingis, a multi-millionaire at 16, said she played "almost perfect tennis" in the second set against American Lisa Raymond to triumph 6-4 6-2.
